bell_tower.note: Tower is a square shaft with identical faces (clocks on all four sides); compass of the photographed face is unknown (sun-lit left face, golden hour), so every face may use the same two tiles.

all_faces.part: brick shaft bay between two limestone ledges (lower shaft; ledge spacing about 5.9 m)
all_faces.attribution: Julian Herzog, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
all_faces.notes: Rectified by cropping the lit face (telephoto, vertical edges parallel) and stretching x by 1/cos33. Scale from brick course pitch (12px = 76 mm), +-15%. Vertical dark seam is a real expansion joint. Face is lit, opposite face in shadow.

all_faces.part: limestone clock stage incl. clock face, cornice, louvre hood
all_faces.attribution: Julian Herzog, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
all_faces.notes: Same method. Baked sun shading and the 3D louvre hood at the bottom are projected flat; clock hands show ~8:15, baked in. Bell chamber arches above are not included.

unassigned_to_compass.part: wall with paired double-hung windows, upper two storeys, between stringcourse and cornice
unassigned_to_compass.notes: Source photo is only 800x887 (about 13 px/m at the near edge), so the tile is upsampled ~2.5x and soft. Metric aspect 1.93 from vanishing-point camera model (f=674px, corner bisected at 45 deg), absolute height ASSUMED 10.2 m. Compass face NOT known (photo is of one WALC corner; its two faces are these two). Use as generic WALC brick/window look, not as an exact face.

unassigned_to_compass.part: wall with tall slit window bays (3 bays recessed) and dark brick, upper two storeys
unassigned_to_compass.notes: Source photo is only 800x887 (about 13 px/m at the near edge), so the tile is upsampled ~2.5x and soft. Metric aspect 5.18 from vanishing-point camera model (f=674px, corner bisected at 45 deg), absolute height ASSUMED 10.2 m. Compass face NOT known (photo is of one WALC corner; its two faces are these two). Use as generic WALC brick/window look, not as an exact face.

walc.note: No photo of WALC with a known compass face was found (Mapillary has none within 40 m, Commons has no WALC file). Faces N/E/S/W are empty; the two unassigned tiles are one corner of the real building, orientation unknown.

brick_red.attribution: Julian Herzog, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
brick_red.notes: Real Purdue Bell Tower red-brown brick (rectified lit face, between the expansion joints), edge cross-faded with a half-shifted copy to tile (slight ghosting in the middle bands). Contains faint real vertical joint lines about every 0.6 m and a darker left edge, so it reads as striped when tiled.

limestone_cream.attribution: Julian Herzog, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
limestone_cream.notes: Plain cream limestone panel beside the clock; small and low-contrast, edge cross-faded.

brick_dark.attribution: Image by kennystier, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Mapillary. Share-alike: needs-clearance
brick_dark.notes: Dark purple-brown brick of Elliott Hall of Music (a different building; Purdue standard dark brick). tile_m set below from course pitch. Scale from ~23px per brick course (76 mm) read by eye; oblique view so +-30%.

limestone_ashlar.attribution: Image by kennystier, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Mapillary. Share-alike: needs-clearance
limestone_ashlar.notes: Grey-buff ashlar limestone base of Elliott Hall (different building; oblique view, sunlit part). tile_m is a guess (course height ~0.4 m).

glass_window.notes: WALC cream-framed glazing, about 40x90 px in the source: upsampled and soft, reflections baked in. Prefer a procedural glass material; kept only as a colour reference.
